verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचइदं तु ते गुह्यतमं प्रवक्ष्याम्यनसूयवे । ज्ञानं विज्ञानसहितं यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: I will now tell you this most secret knowledge, joined with direct realization, to you who are not envious. Knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful.
verses.angle: Anasyave: the condition for the deepest secret
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on by saying he will reveal the deepest teaching, but only because Arjuna has no envy.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: I will now tell you this most secret knowledge, joined with direct realization, to you who are not envious. Knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful. Listen to the word anasyave, without envy. Krishna offers a guarded secret, knowledge joined with realization, to a student who is free from hostility. He calls it the king of all secrets, supremely pure and directly knowable.

verses.sa: राजविद्या राजगुह्यं पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् । प्रत्यक्षावगमं धर्म्यं सुसुखं कर्तुमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: This is the king of all knowledge, the king of all secrets. It is supremely pure, directly knowable, aligned with dharma, easy to practice, and imperishable.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has promised a secret that frees the listener. Now he describes its nature. What makes this knowledge different from ordinary learning?

body.text: This is the king of all knowledge, the king of all secrets. It is supremely pure, directly knowable, aligned with dharma, easy to practice, and imperishable. The word rajaguhyam, king of secrets, marks this knowledge as supreme. It is also abhyayam, imperishable, meaning it never fades away. Krishna then warns those who lack shraddha, trust, in this dharma and remain bound to rebirth.

verses.sa: अश्रद्दधानाः पुरुषा धर्मस्यास्य परन्तप । अप्राप्य मां निवर्तन्ते मृत्युसंसारवर्त्मनि ॥
verses.tr: O conqueror of foes, people without trust in this dharma do not reach Me and keep returning on the path of repeated death and rebirth.
verses.angle: Asradaddhanah: the price of lacking trust
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just called this teaching the king of all secrets. Now he warns what happens to those who receive it without trust.

body.text: O conqueror of foes, people without trust in this dharma do not reach Me and keep returning on the path of repeated death and rebirth. Listen to the word asradaddhanah, without trust. Krishna says people who lack this trust do not reach him and remain on the path of repeated death and rebirth. He then explains that the entire universe is pervaded by his unmanifest form, yet he does not dwell in beings.

verses.sa: मया ततमिदं सर्वं जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना । मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ॥
verses.tr: All this universe is pervaded by my unmanifest form. All beings dwell in me, but I do not dwell in them.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes his form not as a shape you can see, but as an unseen presence. Listen to the word that names this unseen presence.

body.text: All this universe is pervaded by my unmanifest form. All beings dwell in me, but I do not dwell in them. Listen to the word avyaktamurti, unmanifest form. It names the very ground that holds the entire world, yet it is not a thing you can look at or touch. Krishna then turns to the paradox of how all beings rest in him, while he remains beyond them.

verses.sa: न च मत्स्थानि भूतानि पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम् । भूतभृन्न च भूतस्थो ममात्मा भूतभावनः ॥
verses.tr: Behold My divine power: beings are not in Me, and yet I sustain all beings.
verses.angle: My self is not in beings, yet I sustain them
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just told Arjuna that the universe is pervaded by his unmanifest form. Now he asks Arjuna to look closer at how beings relate to his self.

body.text: Behold My divine power: beings are not in Me, and yet I sustain all beings. Krishna offers a direct paradox: My self is not situated in beings, yet I am the source and nourisher of all beings. Krishna then offers the wind and space as an example of how beings rest in him.

verses.sa: यथाऽऽकाशस्थितो नित्यं वायुः सर्वत्रगो महान् । तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय ॥
verses.tr: As the great wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in Me.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues the thread of divine presence by giving a physical image. Listen to the wind and the space and what they mean.

body.text: As the great wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in Me. The wind is everywhere, yet it never leaves the space it moves through, and the verse asks Arjuna to see every being resting in Krishna just as the wind rests in space. Krishna then explains what happens to all beings when a cosmic cycle ends and begins again.

verses.sa: सर्वभूतानि कौन्तेय प्रकृतिं यान्ति मामिकाम् । कल्पक्षये पुनस्तानि कल्पादौ विसृजाम्यहम् ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kunti, at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings enter my nature; at its beginning, I send them forth again.
verses.angle: What seems like ending is only a return before another beginning.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks Arjuna to look beyond the single war to the rhythm of the cosmos. Listen to the two moments that frame every life.

body.text: O son of Kunti, at the end of a cosmic cycle all beings enter my nature; at its beginning, I send them forth again. Kunteya, O son of Kunti, is the address, and it turns a cosmic law into a conversation between teacher and student. Krishna tells Arjuna that all beings rest in his nature at the end of a kalpa and he sends them forth again at its start. He then explains that he takes hold of his own nature to create this multitude of beings again and again.

verses.sa: प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य विसृजामि पुनः पुनः । भूतग्राममिमं कृत्स्नमवशं प्रकृतेर्वशात् ॥
verses.tr: Taking hold of my own nature, I repeatedly create this entire multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of nature.
verses.angle: Prakritim swam: Krishna holds his own nature
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna widens the view from one battlefield to the whole of creation. Listen for the cycle he describes.

body.text: Taking hold of my own nature, I repeatedly create this entire multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of nature. The word prakritim swam, taking hold of my own nature, shows that Krishna does not force the world into being; he simply uses his own power to set the cycle in motion. He then explains that these repeated acts of creation do not bind him at all.

verses.sa: न च मां तानि कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय । उदासीनवदासीनमसक्तं तेषु कर्मसु ॥
verses.tr: Those actions of creation do not bind me, Dhananjaya, because I remain detached and indifferent to them.
verses.angle: Asakta: the word that shows Krishna stands apart
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just described how he creates the world again and again. Now he tells Arjuna that these actions do not bind him. Listen for the word that shows how he stands apart.

body.text: Those actions of creation do not bind me, Dhananjaya, because I remain detached and indifferent to them. Listen for the word asakta, unattached. Krishna says he remains asakta, unattached, in those actions, which means he does not cling to the creation he himself releases into the world. He follows this by saying he sits as a spectator, udasinavat, like one who is indifferent to what unfolds before him.

verses.sa: मयाऽध्यक्षेण प्रकृतिः सूयते सचराचरम् । हेतुनाऽनेन कौन्तेय जगद्विपरिवर्तते ॥
verses.tr: Nature, under my supervision, brings forth all moving and unmoving beings. Because of this, the world keeps changing, O son of Kunti.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is answering Arjuna's deepest confusion. After saying he is not bound by creation, he now explains how the world actually keeps turning. Listen for the reason.

body.text: Nature, under my supervision, brings forth all moving and unmoving beings. Because of this, the world keeps changing, O son of Kunti. The reason the world keeps turning is hetuna anena, because of this. Krishna says that nature itself gives birth to everything under his watch, and that is why the world changes. Next, Krishna continues.

verses.sa: अवजानन्ति मां मूढा मानुषीं तनुमाश्रितम् । परं भावमजानन्तो मम भूतमहेश्वरम् ॥
verses.tr: Fools despise Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.
verses.angle: Human form hides the Lord of beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues by naming the ones who fail to see him, and how they see him.

body.text: Fools despise Me when I dwell in a human form, not knowing My higher nature as the great Lord of all beings. The deluded see only a human body, mam, and despise Me, missing My parambhavam, My higher nature, as the great Lord of all beings. Krishna next describes the confused minds of those who take shelter in deluding and demonic nature.

verses.sa: मोघाशा मोघकर्माणो मोघज्ञाना विचेतसः । राक्षसीमासुरीं चैव प्रकृतिं मोहिनीं श्रिताः ॥
verses.tr: Those whose hopes, actions, and understanding are all wasted, confused minds take shelter in deluding, demonic, and shadowy nature.
verses.angle: Moha: the root of wasted hopes, actions, and understanding
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Why do some people turn away from truth? Krishna answers with a pattern of collapse. Listen for three words that all mean the same thing: wasted.

body.text: Those whose hopes, actions, and understanding are all wasted, confused minds take shelter in deluding, demonic, and shadowy nature. Notice that the verse repeats a single root idea three times. moha means wasted, and the verse strings moha-asha, moha-karman, and moha-jnana together to show that a confused mind makes every hope, every action, and every thought go to waste. Krishna now turns to the great-minded ones, the ones who rely on a divine nature and worship him with single-pointed minds.

verses.sa: महात्मानस्तु मां पार्थ दैवीं प्रकृतिमाश्रिताः । भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो ज्ञात्वा भूतादिमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings.
verses.angle: Ananyamanasah: minds fixed on nothing else
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna contrasts the deluded with the great-minded. Listen for the kind of mind that can truly see him.

body.text: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings. Ananyamanasah means minds fixed on nothing else. The great-minded do not scatter their attention; they hold it on Krishna alone and worship him as the imperishable source of all beings. Krishna then describes how these steadfast souls worship him through chanting, striving, and bowing.
